content.rationale: Ownership is where S2-own's one attribution path, S2-own-inline's degenerate case, and D2's exact rule meet; this check pins the owned set for array and inline documents, and — since D2 reads each listed path in normal form — that the derived set holds one entry per file under one spelling, so a leading `./`, a run of repeated `/` separators of any length, or an interior `.` component never counts as a second owner. It pins the rest of that normal form too: each `..` folds against the ordinary component before it, so `src/../src/x.rs` and `src/x.rs` are one owned entry, and a normal form in which a `..` survives folding names a place outside the repository and contributes no owned path; what a spelling whose components all fold away owns, and whether absolute refs, symlinks or case are owned, are left unpinned because this standard does not decide them. It reads the loaded document as serde_json, so it is a crate of its own. I1-serde (`orrvsxqq`) fixes the JSON layer the crate is written against — serde and serde_json, the crate's own `Value` and the derive.
